result.rationale: The diff confirms the mechanism: in the next/previous actions, group.set("offset", offset) is committed before `return group.findMembers()`, and findMembers has no failure handler (`.then(...)` only, no `.catch`). On a failed members request, currentPage/totalPages would reflect the committed offset while the members array still holds the prior page's data, with no error surfaced. This is a real, diff-verifiable error-handling defect, though it only manifests on request failure and is minor.

judged_text: next commits group.set("offset", offset) before the findMembers() request resolves — and previous does the same at line 46 — with no rollback and no rejection handler, so a failed request leaves the committed offset in place. When the members request fails after clicking next, currentPage (derived from the pre-committed offset) shows page 2 while the member list still renders page 1's data, and no error is surfaced anywhere — the page indicator and the list content disagree with no way to tell the request failed.
